correctness.rationale: Every one of the 1296 strict four-person preference profiles and all three perfect matchings is exhaustively checked, producing 48 unsolvable profiles in two complete 24-profile orbits. Full-rank pre-deletion Mallows weights are summed exactly over four insertions per agent. The 25-term numerator is independently reconstructed by direct C++ enumeration of all 331776 complete-rank draws. Exact integer polynomial identities validate the rational function and derivative. The reciprocal degree-12 derivative factor has at most two positive roots by Descartes and at least two distinct reciprocal roots, yielding a unique simple interior root; rational signs bracket it. Finite verification is not used as an infinite-size claim.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparisons establish known uniform endpoints and known four-agent unsolvable orbit classes, but do not state the 2026 four-agent full-order Mallows rational unsolvability law, its two-inversion onset, or unique nonmonotone peak. Public enumeration data are a component of the proof and not claimed anew. value.rationale: The model reproduces a real Mallows preference culture used in stable-roommates simulations, and a universal intuition about disorder and unsolvability has a mathematically sharp counterexample: full-order inversion cost two, a unique worst-noise level, and a 1.688-fold rise above the independent-uniform endpoint. This finite exact parameter law is motivated by a genuine asymptotic solvability gap and indicates which low-dimensional dynamics should not be assumed monotone. Its scope remains exactly four agents.
